newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady-weak, pressured by light demand from packers with operating margins deep in the red, livestock dealers and market sources said.
Packers reportedly were losing an average $8.50 per head, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean-Witter Reynolds.
One packer buyer who buys hogs in central Iowa/southern Minnesota said some plants were losing as much as $10 a head.
Many packing plants reduced slaughter the past two weeks in attempts to mend margins and appeared ready to continue cutbacks for another week, sources said.

A ConAgra Inc official on Friday confirmed that slaughter cutbacks would continue at Swift and Co pork plants for the third consecutive week. Swift plants in Marshalltown, Iowa and Worthington, Minn., would be operating at "minimum" hours, said K.T. Miller, ConAgra spokeswoman.
Officials at other pork plants were either unavailable for comment or did not have current information on schedules.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs at plants on Monday could range $57.50-$58.00. Illinois tops at plants could range $56.00-$56.50 and Indiana and Ohio top prices could range $57.00-$57.50, sources there said.
